evidence: Receiving DO2 observations: 11.52 mg/L at t=48.0h collapsing to 4.40 mg/L at t=48.2h, declining to 3.27 mg/L at t=52.0h
Receiving delayed assay P: 3.27 g/L at t=48h (sample), comparable to source batches (3.0-3.1 g/L) prior to the transfer loss
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show no such DO2 collapse after 48h, indicating a receiving-specific transfer failure; physical_forward_model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.49 after change at t=48h

Forward-model comparison at t=52h: keep min DO 1.40 mg/L / 4.4h below limit / 174.8 kg; combined 1.48 mg/L / 4.4h / 181.1 kg; strong_feed_reduction 1.66 mg/L / 2.8h / 203.5 kg (best of bounded options)
strong_feed_reduction retains product mass and avoids stop (stop counts zero production)
args.rationale: A receiving-specific oxygen-transfer failure began at t=48 h: DO2 fell from ~11.5 to ~4.4 mg/L within 0.2 h and continued declining to 3.27 mg/L at t=52 h, on track to breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Source batches show no analogous collapse, confirming a receiving-process anomaly rather than normal trajectory. Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) best preserves feasibility: it cuts oxygen demand most, giving the highest projected minimum DO (~1.66 mg/L), the shortest interval below the oxygen limit (~2.8 h), the smallest oxygen deficit, and the highest retained product mass (~203 kg vs ~175 kg under keep). A stop would forfeit all counted production, and milder options leave longer/ deeper oxygen-limit violations. Recommendation is advisory only; no equipment action is executed.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; all options it evaluated remain nominally infeasible over the horizon, though strong_feed_reduction is the best-bounded and has feasible members in the sensitivity ensemble (min DO range 1.14-2.65 mg/L). The true receiving-process parameters (transfer loss magnitude, biomass state) are hidden, so the projected minimum DO could be better or worse than modeled; continued DO2 monitoring is needed and a stop contingency should be reviewed if DO2 falls near 2.0 mg/L despite intervention.
